AuraConfig__File__Description: ValeVision AURA app config: who may open it, the drawing sheets (paper, border and the Vale title column), viewport scales and frames, the engine parameters the 3D Environment shows, annotations and the handwriting, the render queue and saving. Read by the browser (GET api/config, else this file) and by the AURA API. Keys are Area__Group__Setting; a key ending Note says why.
AuraConfig__App__EngineNote: AURA's core library: Adam's PainterlyNPR pen and wash renderer, pinned in 04__Lib__CoreEngine__VersionLocked (its modules, and the libraries and stylesheets it reads) and reached only through 02__Src__AppModules/10__System__EngineHost. Nothing of it is copied into AURA: what AURA needs from it is a seam in PainterlyNPR, synced.
AuraConfig__Access__MinimumLevelNote: Managers and App Admins only while AURA is new (Adam, 30-Oct-2026): Employees, Affiliates and clients are refused by the page and by every API route, and the Gallery hides the link from them.
AuraConfig__Access__ProjectSwitchNote: Projects too, one by one (Adam, 30-Oct-2026): a project opens only when ticked Available in ValeVision AURA in the Gallery's Project Editor (auraEnabled in its ProjectData, written by the Gallery API). A record without it is off; the Gallery shows no shortcut and every AURA project route refuses it (403, notSwitchedOn).
AuraConfig__Panels__WidthPxNote: The side panels' widths in screen pixels: dragged at their inner edge (ValeVision 3D's Layout Editor grip) between Min and Max, and kept in this browser; Environment is the 3D Environment's panel, SheetLeft and SheetRight the sheets' two panels. Their sections fold and are remembered too.
AuraConfig__ArtDirection__Note: Art direction points are PainterlyNPR's own (its 65__ArtDirection__InfluencePoints: types, defaults, the editor), one set a view (Adam, 30-Oct-2026): a saved view's (shared by every sheet viewport that shows it), the 3D Environment's unsaved view's, and each other viewport's own. A view holds the engine's MaxPoints (8).
AuraConfig__Scene__DemoLabel: PainterlyNPR demo scene: a brick country cottage in its garden
AuraConfig__Scene__DemoNote: Every project opens the engine's demo scene for now. A project's own AURA model arrives with ValeVision Cloud Sync's AURA export (a Painterly Scene Package in the project's ValeVision__AuraRender/Content__AuraScenePackages).
AuraConfig__Sheet__PaperSizesNote: Listed landscape; portrait swaps width and height.
AuraConfig__Sheet__BorderNote: The ruled border, from the paper's edge: Side across the long edges' ends (left and right in landscape), End along the long edges (top and bottom). Measured on Vale's A3 layout (10.6 / 8.2 mm); A1 measures within a millimetre.
AuraConfig__TitleBlock__StyleNote: Vale's standard drawing page (the RecConcept layouts of Feb-2026 that ValeVision 3D's Create Drawing uses): a 60 x 280.5 mm column, the same size on every sheet, at the bottom right inside the border in landscape, turned 90 degrees clockwise to the bottom left in portrait. A4 is too short for it, so there it is scaled down to fit.
AuraConfig__TitleBlock__FixedCellsNote: The logo and Grantham address, the setting-out note and the copyright cell, cut at 300 dpi from Vale's A3 layout: the same physical size on every sheet, so it prints sharp on A1.
AuraConfig__TitleBlock__CellsNote: Column-local millimetres from the column's top left, measured on Vale's A3 layout (the column's top is 8.2 mm down the sheet).
AuraConfig__Viewport__ScaledFrameNote: A scaled view (an elevation or a plan) is one engine frame: the engine draws on its own sheet (A3, 420 x 297 mm since PainterlyNPR 0.8.3, read from the engine), so a scaled viewport is at most that size and its pen widths are true millimetres on the paper. A perspective is drawn for its frame since AURA 0.5.5 (PainterlyNPR 0.8.9): the same framing as the whole sheet sliced into it, at the frame's true size, so its pens are true too; only a frame bigger than the sheet is enlarged. Both have the engine's vignette fitted inside the frame.
AuraConfig__Viewport__RenderDpiNote: Viewport pictures are drawn at this many dots per inch on the paper (Adam: "Documents should be 300 dpi"): the engine's whole A3 sheet at 300 dpi is 4961 x 3508 px, about 5.6 times the pixels of its 5 px/mm screen size and about 2 GB of GPU memory. Pen widths and grain are millimetres, so it is the same drawing, sharper. A GPU that cannot hold it draws the picture at screen size instead (the console says so). Only the frame's part of the sheet is kept (AURA 0.5.5).
AuraConfig__Viewport__PictureCacheMbNote: How much memory the viewports' pictures may take in this browser before the oldest are let go (and drawn again when next shown). They are lossless PNG since AURA 0.5.5, as the engine's own export (WebP at 0.92 halved the colour and smoothed the pens, grain and washes): a 180 x 120 mm frame at 300 dpi is a few megabytes, a whole A3 sheet tens of them. At most forty are kept, whatever their size.
AuraConfig__Viewport__RedrawSettleMsNote: A picture is drawn for its frame, so a resized viewport is drawn again: this long after the frame stops changing, so a drag never waits on the engine. Meanwhile its last picture stands in, pale.
AuraConfig__Viewport__MeasuredCeilingNot: The engine's view profile for a measured drawing: a Natural Pen at most, never a loose one (its MeasuredElevation preset).
AuraConfig__Viewport__PlanPitchDegNote: Straight down, short of 90 degrees so the engine's camera keeps world up as its reference. 0.1 degrees moves a 10 m roof's ridge 17 mm in the world: 0.2 mm on a 1:100 sheet.
AuraConfig__Viewport__ElevationsNote: Yaw is the engine's: 0 looks at the front (+Z) face, 90 at the right (+X) face as seen from the front.
AuraConfig__Cameras__LensNote: The 3D Environment's Cameras section, the lens: ValeVision 3D's (its config's cameraLens), a focal length on a full-frame sensor 24 mm high, turned into the engine camera's vertical field of view (FovY = 2 atan(24 / 2f)). The engine's 30 degrees is a 45 mm lens, ValeVision 3D's default. Elevations and the roof plan are to scale and have none.
AuraConfig__Cameras__CutNote: A scaled scene's cut (View__CutM, its drawing plane): nothing in front of it is drawn. The engine clips at its near plane, 0.1 m from the eye for the wash and 0.2 m for the pen (PainterlyNPR 31__Line__Visibility), so the eye stands CutEyeOffsetM before the plane: the pen stops exactly at it and a face standing on it keeps its lines. A plane at or behind the scene's centre takes the camera's target back, keeping at least CutLeastDistanceM between the eye and the target, so the camera always looks forward. Not cut: the camera stands Viewport__OrthoDistanceM out, as before cuts.
AuraConfig__Cameras__CutAtBuildingNote: Cut elevations at the building (the Cameras section): every elevation's cut this far in front of the face of the building's box (its Architecture and Focal objects, the box the planes are sized from), measured from the building drawn now; the roof plan is left as it is. Adam, 30-Oct-2026: "Offset the cut 50mm infrtont of box plane", the roof plan not cut.
AuraConfig__Cameras__PlaneSnapNote: TrueVision 3D's drawing planes' snap (Na__DrawingPlanes__AppConfig__.json): a plane's ABSOLUTE position along its normal is snapped to the increment from the world origin, never the distance dragged, so every plane shares one grid. The increments are the stepper's steps; the default must be one of them. The viewer's last choice is kept in the browser.
AuraConfig__Cameras__PlaneBoundsNote: How large a plane is drawn, from the building alone (its Architecture and Focal objects), never the garden. The overshoot is how far it runs past the building on each side, where the grips sit clear of it: the larger of OvershootM and OvershootFraction of the building's longer side. An elevation's foot stands GroundLiftM above the building's lowest point. A plane never cut waits an overshoot in front of the building.
AuraConfig__Cameras__PlaneLookNote: What a plane looks like, after TrueVision 3D's: one colour from the palette for its face, outline, grips, name tab and arrows, chosen from the scene's id so deleting a scene never recolours the rest. The face is faint (the building cannot stand in front of it: the planes are drawn over the drawing), brighter while it is under the pointer or dragged, fainter and dashed while not cut. Grips are GripPx boxes on screen; the arrows run ArrowLengthFraction of the building's longer side, between the minimum and maximum, the way the drawing looks.
AuraConfig__Cameras__PlaneDragNote: A drag is solved as the point on the plane's normal nearest the pointer's ray, so a plane never slides sideways. Within MinAxisAngleDeg of the view the solve turns a pixel into metres, so the plane holds still and the readout asks for another angle; in an elevation or the plan a plane that square on is not drawn at all.
AuraConfig__Engine__OwnSectionsNote: The 3D Environment's parameters are PainterlyNPR's own panel (80__System__HudOverlay/Na__Interface__Panel__Config.json, read through 10__System__EngineHost): every section, group, fold, slider, menu, preset and hint, in the engine's order and words. AURA leaves out only the sections it has its own of: Camera (its saved views), ArtDirection (its Art direction points section) and Export (its drawing sheets). Since AURA 0.3.3 (Adam: "ensure all parameters are availible from npr in aura", "dont duplicate code the npr repo remains definitive source").
AuraConfig__Annotation__InksNote: The Vale Handwriting Studio's own ink presets (Forest is its default), and Vale navy.

AuraConfig__Handwriting__PensNote: The four calibrated technical pens of PainterlyNPR's pen guidance (08__Data__StrokeLibrary/PainterlyNPR__PenPresets__PointWeights__.md), with the same keys and fields as the engine's 32__Line__ClassAndPriority/Na__TechnicalPens__Config.json, so notes and linework use one pen set. Widths are absolute: millimetres on the printed sheet. The sheet is drawn in paper millimetres, so a note's pen is its true width when the sheet prints at 100% on its own paper; printed on a smaller paper it shrinks with it (the panel says how far). Adam, 30-Oct-2026: "the artists use a 0.18mm fineline ... STAEDTLER Mars matic 700".
AuraConfig__Handwriting__DefaultPenNote: Lettering is the 0.18 mm tier (the guidance). The pen is applied on the sheet, like the ink's colour, so a new pen redraws a note at once, without writing it again; its leader takes the same pen.
AuraConfig__Handwriting__LetteringNote: The sheet's own words written by hand (Adam, 30-Oct-2026: "Use handwriting in the titleblock and viewports not text"): the title block's entries (its labels and Vale's artwork stay printed) and every viewport's title. ONE PEN FOR THE WHOLE SHEET (AURA 0.5.10; Adam: "all the text on the page ... looks like it was written by the same person with the same pen at the same time"): the house standard is the Example Cottage's leader note, so the lettering writes as a new note does: the Steady hand (with its StepsPerChar and MinNeatness), architect's capitals, the 0.18 mm M018 and Forest ink. Hand: one of the hands above. Ink: one of the note inks (Annotation__Inks). Pen: the lettering pen; EmphasisPen where the typed block was bold (the title and the drawing number), the same M018 since 0.5.10. A viewport's title is written at a note's height (Annotation__DefaultSizeMm). SizeFactor: the handwriting's letter height over the typed size it replaces (a handwritten phrase's height runs from its tallest letter to its lowest, a typed size from its em). Style: any writing style key, as a note's own. Written once on each device and kept there (31__System__Handwriting/Na__Handwriting__Lettering__.js); typed until written.
AuraConfig__Handwriting__HandsNote: Neatness is the model's bias (the studio calls it pen confidence, 0.2 to 2.5); Variation varies slant, baseline and pen weight (0 to 1). A hand may set any writing style key below (its Key and a value): the rest keep their defaults. The model has no style index: a note's own seed makes it a different hand-written copy. The Steady hand is the house standard (AURA 0.5.10), read from the Example Cottage's leader note: StepsPerChar 150 and MinNeatness 0.75 over the studio's defaults; new notes, the title block and the viewport titles all write with it.
AuraConfig__Handwriting__LettersNote: A note's letters (Annotation__Letters, else DefaultLetters). Capitals: drawn single-stroke architect's capitals, lettered at once on the page with no model (Adam, 30-Oct-2026: "the writing needs to be like image 03, all caps (but can do regular) but neat"); a capital stands 0.7 of the letter height. Joined: the Graves model's joined-up hand, which cannot write capitals. The lettering (title block and viewport titles) takes its own Letters, and CapitalsSizeFactor for its letter height over the typed size.

Controls.Label: Neatness
Controls.Hint: The model's bias: higher writes neater, more predictable letters; lower, looser and more varied ones. The hand's own value until changed here.

Controls.Label: Tries
Controls.Hint: How many times a phrase is written again when the pen stalls or skips a letter.

Controls.Label: Retry neatness
Controls.Hint: Each retry writes with the neatness times this, so a stalled pen is shaken loose. 1 retries with the same neatness.

Controls.Label: Lowest neatness
Controls.Hint: Retries never write below this neatness.

Controls.Label: Letter check
Controls.Hint: Pen steps each letter and digit must hold the model's attention, or the phrase is tried again (a skipped letter). Not a spelling check; 0 turns it off.

Controls.Label: Steps a character
Controls.Hint: Pen steps allowed for each character before a phrase counts as stalled.

Controls.Label: Fewest steps
Controls.Hint: Pen steps allowed even for a short phrase.

Controls.Label: Most steps
Controls.Hint: The most pen steps any phrase may take (the engine's own limit is 6500).

Controls.Label: Line spacing
Controls.Hint: Letter heights from one line to the next.

Controls.Label: Longest phrase
Controls.Hint: The most characters the pen writes in one go; a longer line is split between words. The model tires on long phrases (the studio's 42).

Controls.Label: Shortest phrase
Controls.Hint: The fewest characters a line is wrapped to, even in a narrow note.

Controls.Label: Wrap
Controls.Hint: Characters to one letter height across the note, for the first wrap by words; the written ink is then fitted to the width.

Controls.Label: Word gap
Controls.Hint: A space between words in capitals, and between words and numbers in a joined-up note, in letter heights.

Controls.Label: Space width
Controls.Hint: Each further space where several are typed together, in letter heights.

Controls.Label: Space before
Controls.Hint: Extra space before words that follow a number in a joined-up note, in letter heights.

Controls.Label: Margin
Controls.Hint: Paper left round the words inside the note.

Controls.Label: Variation
Controls.Hint: The overall amount of slant, baseline wave and (with a variable pen) weight swing. The hand's own value until changed here.

Controls.Label: Slant spread
Controls.Hint: How far each phrase's slant varies, times the variation.

Controls.Label: Baseline wave
Controls.Hint: How far the baseline rises and falls, in letter heights, times the variation.

Controls.Label: Wave frequency
Controls.Hint: How quickly the baseline wave rises and falls along a line.

Controls.Label: Straighten tilt
Controls.Hint: The most overall tilt taken out of each phrase; 0 keeps the model's own.

Controls.Label: Pen width
Controls.Hint: A Mars matic draws one width, as the pen guidance asks. Variable swings each stroke's weight round the nib, as the studio did: a non-technical look. The leader follows the same pen.

Controls.Label: Weight swing
Controls.Hint: Variable pen only: how far a stroke's weight swings, times the variation.

Controls.Label: Draw numbers exactly
Controls.Hint: Numbers, units and drawing symbols drawn with explicit strokes, so a dimension is exactly what was typed. Off, the model writes the digits itself.

Controls.Label: Copy number
Controls.Hint: The note's seed: the same words, settings and number always write the same strokes. Write a new copy picks another.

AuraConfig__Handwriting__StyleGroupsNote: The Advanced writing style in a note's panel: every setting of the writing model and the studio's layout, a note at a time (Adam, 30-Oct-2026: "exposing all of the possible paramers for the writing model"; per note, starting from its hand). Default is the studio's own value; the hand's value wins where it has one; a note keeps only what was changed in it (Annotation__Style), and choosing a hand clears that. The engine clamps every value to its own hard limits (02__Engine__Wasm/Na__HandwritingEngine__Layout__.js, Na__Layout__STYLE).
AuraConfig__Handwriting__WhereItRuns: In the browser, on the user's own machine, never on the server (Adam, 30-Oct-2026: the server is resource constrained; "Refactor the Handwriting tool from python to WASM"): the studio's Graves model in WebAssembly (31__System__Handwriting/02__Engine__Wasm), in a Web Worker. The AURA API only hands over its model (api/handwriting/model and api/handwriting/weights/<sha256>, Managers and App Admins only), which the worker keeps on the device after the first note. A note shows a typed stand-in only until it is written, or where the engine cannot run.
AuraConfig__Handwriting__ModelNote: The Vale Handwriting Studio's checkpoint (X-rayLaser/pytorch-handwriting-synthesis-toolkit at 899e9432, Epoch_46), its 32-bit weights as they are (15 MB; Adam, 30-Oct-2026: "32-bit, 15 MB"). Trained on IAM-OnDB, an evaluation asset: served to signed-in staff only, never committed. Rebuilt by 60__Dev__WebBuildUtils/AuraRender__BuildUtil__HandwritingWeights__.py into Server__Api/Api__ValeVision__AuraRender/Content__AuraHandwritingModel.
AuraConfig__History__MaxNote: Adam, 30-Oct-2026: '100 undos and 100 redos'. One history for the whole drawing set (his call), kept in the browser for this visit only: the oldest step goes when a 101st is made, and a new edit after an undo clears the steps forward. The keys are 40__Feature__DrawingSet/Na__Hotkeys__DrawingSet__.json.
AuraConfig__History__SettleNote: An announced edit becomes a step once nothing more has changed for SettleMs and no pointer button is held, so a drag is one step; in a text box TypingSettleMs, or when the box is left, so a run of typing is one step.

AuraConfig__SceneImport__Rules.UseNote: ValeVision 3D's orbit helper cube: never drawn
SketchUp's own edges for the mesh twin's objects: the engine's hard edges, node for node (PainterlyNPR 10__Import__ScenePackage, Glb)

AuraConfig__SceneImport__Note: How AURA's import (the API: POST api/projects/<id>/scene/import) reads ValeVision 3D's whitecard, by file name (<project>__TrueVision__<Group>__<Variant>__<Kind>Model__.glb): the first rule whose every condition the file meets (Match: in its Id; Kind: Mesh or Linework; Group; VariantStarts; VariantContains) gives its Use (Draw, SourceLinework, Ignore) and its objects' starting Role, Category and material class; a component node's type word (<code>__Column__...) can override those; SkipNodes are TrueVision's drawing notes, never objects. The material is where an object starts: the drawing set's material assignments paint the rest. Provisional values (30-Oct-2026), Adam to set: AuraRender__SCHEMA__AuraScene__.md.
AuraConfig__History__ChunkNote: Parts of a step this long or longer (as JSON) are stored once and shared by every step that holds them (03__AppUtils Snapshot Store): a handwritten note's pen paths are kept once, however many steps it is in.
